To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the interpretation of CVS is improved when direct studies are used to identify non-fetal cell lines and the study of cultures is always done.

the combined use of direct chorionic villi study and cell cultures always uncovers the non-fetal source of chromosome abnormalities and that the study of cultured chorionic villi cells in all cases can prevent 5 terminations.
the combined use of direct chorionic villi and cultured cells in all mosaic studies can nearly 100% accurately detect non-fetal chromosome abnormalities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of fetal chromosome anomalies by chorionic villus sampling and the evaluation of fetal karyotypes by direct studies and cell cultures.
the interpretation of chromosome mosaics, the origin of non-fetal cell lines, and the accuracy of CVS.

the following: 1. the frequency of chromosome mosaism and the origin of the mosaicism; 2. the interpretation of chromosome mosaics and the use of direct and cultured cells for the detection of mosaics and other cell lines; and 3. the accuracy of CVS in the diagnosis of chromosome abnormalities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CVS results were correct in 98.8% of cases.
the risk of fetal aneuploids is 0.3% (1/333) in cases of molar pregnancy and that the risk of aneuploides is 2% (6/300) in cases of normal pregnancy.
CVS has a high accuracy and is a safe method of prenatal diagnosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in 3,000 CVS, 40 (1.3%) cases of mosaics and 7 false cell lines (0.2%) were seen.
CVS is an accurate method of diagnosing fetal abnormalities, but the results must be interpreted carefully and the studies of direct CVS and cultured cells must be examined together.
in 3,000 cases of CVS, 7 false-positive and 3 false-negative results were seen.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CVS is a reliable diagnostic test for prenatal diagnosis of genetic disorders, and it can be performed safely.

CVS can be nearly perfect if both direct studies and cell cultures are examined in all cases of mosaics, and other cell lines with possible non-fetal origins, including trisomies 16 and 18, translocations (21;21) and 45,X.
in all cases of mosaics and other possible non-fetal cell lines, the combined use of direct studies and cultures is necessary to avoid false-positive results.
